BORROWING COSTS RISE AS INVESTORS FRET Highlighting investor concern over the situation, French government borrowing costs have jumped this week, pushing benchmark 10-year bond yields to 5%, [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"their highest level"] since July 2002. Analysts said the move reflected worries that the unrest could complicate government efforts to repair strained public finances at a time of already mounting budget pressures. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met union leaders in an effort to defuse the crisis, but there was no sign of a breakthrough, with labour groups saying they had received no concrete response to their demands on wages and public services. "There has been no consideration whatsoever of our demands," said Sophie Binet, head of the left-wing CGT group. "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level," she added, confirming next month's national strike. The protests reflect a deeper malaise in France, where high energy costs, pressure on household budgets and concerns about the state of public services have fed a growing sense of frustration among workers and young people. A second consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas hit by the mayhem, offering the government some respite as it prepared for fresh demonstrations. Government ministers have promised a vastly reinforced security operation this coming Saturday after acknowledging shortcomings in their initial response, with troops expected to be deployed alongside additional police. Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said on Wednesday around 2,500 people had been taken into custody following the October 17 protests, adding that 917 suspects had been referred for prosecution and 174 people already jailed. PROTESTS ELSEWHERE IN EUROPE The unrest has triggered a political backlash ahead of presidential elections next year, with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls. "The government has lost control of everything," far-right leader Marine Le Pen told Franceinfo radio. The hard-left France Unbowed (LFI), which has denied allegations by ministers of fueling the unrest, criticised plans to deploy troops on the streets of Paris. "Demonstrators are not enemies within. The French government must not go to war against its own people," LFI's parliamentary group said in a statement. Protests in other European countries have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading at a time when many nations are struggling with budget woes. In Greece, thousands of [USN:L6N4660T6 TEXT:"students and teachers"] took to the streets on Wednesday, demanding higher state funding for education, better facilities and less-crowded classrooms, echoing protesters in other European countries. Meanwhile [USN:L8N4661X4 TEXT:"Italy approved"] a raft of security measures on Tuesday, including a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration and tougher penalties for rioters in response to turbulence last weekend.

item.title: Elevance lifts 2026 profit forecast on disciplined cost management
item.description: Elevance Health on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results, helped by lower medical costs.
item.dc:creator: Sneha K, Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: Elevance Health (ELV.N) on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results, helped by lower medical costs. Health insurers have been navigating declining membership, as well as rising costs in government-backed plans. Elevance, like other health insurers, has adjusted its pricing to reflect higher medical costs. For the third quarter, the company said higher premium yields and service fees offset lower membership, helping the company's insurance business post a $1.1 billion rise in revenue from a year earlier. Elevance forecast full-year adjusted profit to be at least $29 per share, compared with its previous outlook of at least $27 per share. Analysts on average estimate an annual profit of $27.23 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. "Our earnings foundation is stronger, and we're entering 2027 with greater visibility and greater momentum," CEO Gail Boudreaux said in a conference call with analysts. For 2027, the company expects to deliver at least 12% growth in adjusted profit when compared to its earnings baseline of at least $26.75 per share. The company's adjusted quarterly profit was $6.99 per share, above expectations of $4.68 per share. Baird analyst Michael Ha said although Elevance delivered a large beat-and-raise, the smaller lift to recurring earnings leaves the stock vulnerable to a fade. Shares were down 1.3% in morning trading, after rising roughly 2% premarket post results. LOWER MEDICAL COSTS For the third quarter, the health insurer reported a medical loss ratio, the percentage of premiums spent on medical care, of 90.6%, better than analysts' expectations of 91.17%. The company said lower costs were due to better performance across its government-backed plans compared to the prior year. The company expects Medicaid margins to improve in 2027 as reimbursement rates become better aligned with elevated cost trends. Meanwhile, membership at its insurance unit declined by 487,000 compared with last year to about 44.9 million as of September 30, the company said. The company also named Jeff Park as president of Carelon, its health services business, effective December 1. "Carelon's pharmacy and services businesses are growing earnings while managing a larger share of the health plans' medical spending. That supports management's integrated strategy and helps offset pressure on insurance profits," said Daniel Barasa, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds. The unit reported operating revenue of $19.3 billion, an increase of $1 billion from the prior year.

item.title: For Flavio Bolsonaro, runoff vote tests Brazilians' appetite for family's political brand
item.description: For right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, his biggest strength is also his greatest weakness: the Bolsonaro family name.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: For right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, his biggest strength is also his greatest weakness: the Bolsonaro family name. While supporters across Brazil consider him a more moderate iteration of his father's powerful conservative brand, many others view him as a continuation of Jair Bolsonaro's scorched-earth rule that polarized the nation and culminated in an [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"attempted coup"] after he lost the 2022 election. So far, more voters seem willing to test the first hypothesis, with Bolsonaro heading into Sunday's run-off as the [USN:S8N442025 TEXT:"frontrunner"] against incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. A Bolsonaro victory would shift Brazil sharply rightward after four years of leftist rule, and likely push Latin America's largest nation closer into the orbit of the United States led by President [USN:S0N3ZY04Q TEXT:"Donald Trump"]. DISSATISFACTION WITH LULA Flavio's unexpected candidacy caught both insiders and markets off guard, especially since lingering corruption allegations — which he denies — and a crowded conservative field appeared to complicate his path to the presidency. But analysts say he has capitalized on growing [USN:L2N3QG01R TEXT:"dissatisfaction"] with 80-year-old Lula, while also tapping into his father's conservative coalition of powerful farmers, big business and evangelicals. Flavio, who is himself a converted evangelical, says that running for president felt like a calling after his father was sentenced to 27 years in prison for coup-plotting, a sentence he is now serving under house arrest. "I understand that everything happening is God's plan for our nation," [USN:L6N3XR02X TEXT:"he told Reuters"] late last year just after announcing his bid with his father's blessing. Murilo Miranda, a 42-year-old physician who attended a recent Bolsonaro rally in Sao Paulo, said Lula had overseen a system of welfare handouts and a bulging bureaucracy that had hindered Brazilian growth and led to endemic corruption. "They think the state is a father figure that is going to save them," Miranda told Reuters. Hermano Silveira, a 51-year-old contractor who was also at the rally, said Flavio was a new political force. "He is a young guy and we want change," Silveira said. RESOLVE HIS FATHER'S LEGAL PROBLEMS Bolsonaro has sought to acknowledge his father's missteps in power while tapping into his fervent base. During the first debate with Lula, he recognized his father's mishandled COVID-19 response, seeking to address a frequent line of attack. "Healthcare was not an area in which we achieved our best results under President Bolsonaro," he said. "I make this mea culpa here today." However, Bolsonaro has been clear that if he wins, he will quickly resolve his father's legal troubles. "I ask God for the opportunity to walk up the ramp of Planalto Palace next year alongside President Jair Messias Bolsonaro, so that he may place the presidential sash across my chest," he said on the campaign trail. So far, Bolsonaro has announced only one cabinet choice, naming Claudio Lottenberg, the former head of the private Albert Einstein hospital, as his pick for health minister. While promising to [USN:L1N4610Z9 TEXT:"cut spending"], Flavio has also pledged to boost public services and protect social welfare benefits for the population.

item.title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
item.description: As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology. OpenAI’s safety practices have been in the spotlight in recent months, after the company said a swarm of its AI agents escaped containment and [USN:L6N44N119 TEXT:"hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face"]. OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US [USN:L1N45K0VR TEXT:"President Donald Trump’s voluntary AI safety agreement"] on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with "independent auditors" and to ensure their AI tools do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways." Yet Leading the Future, a political group backed with a $25 million donation from Brockman and his wife, Anna, opposes regulations that “unduly constrain or delay AI development” in the US. The group is spending millions to influence the outcome of at least 48 races for US House and Senate seats. INDUSTRY PROFITS VERSUS REGULATION Brockman’s backing prompted criticism from AI safety advocates, who say it raises questions about whether OpenAI executives genuinely want the US government to impose requirements on powerful AI systems. Federal government requirements could hurt the industry's profits if they slow the release of new models or prompt the companies to change how their products perform to address security concerns. OpenAI and rival Anthropic are [USN:L1N4610T9 TEXT:"laying the groundwork for public offerings"] that are expected to rank among the largest ever. “There are leaders in industry who want to pay lip service to regulation because they realize where public opinion is,” said Charlie Blaettler of Guardrails Alliance, a political group formed to counter Leading the Future. “But they're the same leaders who stood up a super PAC whose sole purpose was to oppose candidates who stand up for regulation.” OpenAI said in a blog post that the Brockmans' donation was in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the company. Greg Brockman's personal spokesperson declined to comment on his donations. In a post on X from 2025, Brockman said that "being pro-AI does not mean being anti-regulation. It means being thoughtful." Leading the Future’s spokesperson, Jesse Hunt, did not address the donation in a statement, saying the group seeks "champions who can work together in Congress to advance a strong, responsible national regulatory AI framework." The New York Times reported in September that the Brockmans backed out of a pledge to donate another $25 million to Leading the Future. Leading the Future declined to comment on the New York Times' reporting. FEDERAL LAW TO PRE-EMPT STATE AI LAWS Other contributors to Leading the Future include Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, who, along with their venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, gave a combined $50 million to the group, according to Federal Election Commission records. Andreessen Horowitz is an investor in OpenAI. One of the candidates Leading the Future is backing is Republican Andy Barr, who is running to represent Kentucky in the Senate. Barr told the newspaper the Lexington Herald-Leader in March that he supports federal legislation that would block individual states from passing or enforcing their own regulations on AI, a concept known as pre-emption. Build American AI, a nonprofit group affiliated with Leading the Future, has run advertisements on social media platforms calling on Congress to pass a national standard for AI, rather than allowing states to pass their own rules. Leading the Future also sent funds to Republicans Julia Letlow, who is running for Senate in Louisiana, and Amanda McKinney, a candidate for Congress in Washington state. Both say on their campaign websites that they are opposed to "heavy-handed" regulation of the AI sector. OpenAI rival Anthropic has [USN:L6N43N198 TEXT:"given at least $40 million"] to Public First Action, a political action committee that is against federal pre-emption laws. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called federal pre-emption of state rules [USN:L3N3S80QH TEXT:""too blunt""].

item.title: Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen released by Russia?
item.description: Here are details of Hubbard's case.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Papachristou
item.content:encoded: President Vladimir Putin announced the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russian detention on Wednesday, [USN:L6N4670LA TEXT:"at the start of talks"] with US special envoy Steve Witkoff. Here are details of Hubbard's case: WHO IS STEPHEN HUBBARD? Hubbard, 74, a retired schoolteacher, grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by the New York Times. He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izyum in eastern Ukraine with a Ukrainian partner, according to his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox. Fox told Reuters in 2024 that Hubbard subsisted on a pension of about $300 a month and had few connections with local people. The siblings last spoke in September 2021. HOW WAS HE CAPTURED? Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022 and captured Izyum two months later. Ukrainian forces retook the city in September 2022, but Hubbard was already in Russian custody by then. Russian state media said Hubbard had been detained in April 2022 and alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture. Fox said she recognised her brother in a YouTube video showing a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. Another video showed him with his hands bound, being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the videos were recorded. WHY WAS HE IMPRISONED? Following a closed trial, a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary in October 2024 and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison.Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month. Russian state media said he had pleaded guilty to the charges he faced. Fox questioned the reported confession, however, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian views and was unlikely to have taken up arms in his seventies. Martin De Luca, his US-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit. He cited Hubbard as telling him Russian soldiers had simply grabbed him from his house. WHAT IS HUBBARD'S CURRENT STATUS? In January 2025, Washington designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained, enabling the US government to pursue negotiations for his release. The State Department has said Russia refused to grant US officials consular access. The New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been moved through at least five Russian detention centres before his trial. His lawyer said Hubbard's legal team found out only in April 2025 that he was being held in a facility in the Mordovia region, east of Moscow.

item.title: Gobierno de Colombia fijará por decreto presupuesto para 2027 por error de trámite en el Congreso
item.description: El Gobierno de Colombia fijará por decreto el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (200.679 millones de dólares), después de que el proyecto de ley aprobado por el Congreso se hundió por un vicio de trámite, anunció el miércoles el vicepresidente, José Manuel Restrepo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Colombia fijará por decreto el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (200.679 millones de dólares), después de que el proyecto de ley aprobado por el Congreso se hundió por un vicio de trámite, anunció el miércoles el vicepresidente, José Manuel Restrepo. La cifra total, que supera los 555,8 billones de pesos del presupuesto vigente para 2026, no cambiará frente a la aprobada por el Congreso. "El Gobierno Nacional, en el día de hoy, procederá a decretar dicho Presupuesto General de la Nación", dijo Restrepo en una declaración, al destacar que incluye todos los gastos sociales y de funcionamiento del Estado. El presupuesto prevé un déficit fiscal récord de 9,4% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB), en medio de fuertes necesidades de financiamiento, que incluso llevaron al presidente Abelardo De La Espriella a buscar apoyo del Fondo Monetario Internacional. El Senado aprobó el proyecto de ley de presupuesto el lunes en la noche con 57 votos a favor y uno en contra, mientras que la Cámara de Representantes lo hizo el martes en la madrugada con 112 votos a favor y uno en contra. Uno de los artículos del presupuesto fue aprobado en la Cámara de Representantes con un contenido diferente al del Senado, lo que, según congresistas, vició todo el trámite del proyecto de ley. Al ser aprobados textos diferentes, debió darse una conciliación entre la Cámara y el Senado, trámite que no se realizó antes de la fecha límite del 20 de octubre. "Regirá el proyecto que el Gobierno presentó con las modificaciones aprobadas y discutidas por el Congreso en el primer debate", aseguró el vicepresidente. "Tanto el monto de 634,9 billones de pesos, como la distribución que el Congreso estudió y aprobó en primer debate, quedaron aprobados, así como también las facultades de traslado y de reorientación presupuestal", explicó el funcionario. El presupuesto que había sido aprobado por el Senado y la Cámara de Representantes contemplaba una reasignación de recursos entre diferentes sectores, con recortes en rubros relacionados con el acuerdo de paz e incrementos en los recursos para el pago del servicio de la deuda y para salud. Al hundirse el proyecto, esa reasignación no se aplicará, según congresistas. Con el proyecto presentado por el Gobierno, el recorte al presupuesto de funcionamiento de la Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz (JEP), creada en virtud del acuerdo de paz de 2016 firmado con la antigua guerrilla de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC), será menor que el propuesto, según legisladores. Restrepo envió un mensaje de tranquilidad a los inversionistas, tenedores de bonos y a la comunidad financiera internacional y aseguró que el presupuesto recoge el esfuerzo de ajuste fiscal que necesita el país. El vicepresidente anunció que próximamente se presentará al Congreso la "Ley de Rescate" para organizar las finanzas publicas y garantizar el crecimiento de la economía. (1 dólar = 3.163,76 pesos)

item.title: Netflix's ad stumble deepens fears its growth is hitting a wall
item.description: Netflix's cut to its advertising sales forecast is fuelling concerns that its growth engine is losing steam, threatening the edge that made it a model for the media industry.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Kanishka Ajmera
item.content:encoded: Netflix's (NFLX.O) cut to its advertising sales forecast is fuelling concerns that its growth engine is losing steam, threatening the edge that made it a model for the media industry. Shares of the company fell nearly 5% in Wednesday afternoon trading after Netflix forecast a fourth consecutive quarter of slowing revenue growth, as one of Hollywood's biggest spenders on original content struggles to deliver major hits. "Netflix is increasingly being judged against its own exceptionally high standards, raising questions about whether it has lost some of the focus and agility that once distinguished it from rivals," PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore wrote in a client note. The stock has lost about a quarter of its value this year, with Netflix's failed pursuit of Warner Bros Discovery adding to concerns that it is running out of avenues for growth beyond price increases and its crackdown on password sharing. Netflix's advertising business, long seen as a key source of future growth, is expanding more slowly than expected, while its push into gaming, backed by deals including one to add some "Grand Theft Auto" titles, has yet to make a meaningful contribution. Meanwhile, YouTube and TikTok are competing for viewers with a steady stream of relatively inexpensive user-generated content, while the combination of Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount under Skydance is set to intensify competition. Netflix has responded by cutting 6% of its workforce and replacing two top programming executives. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said on Tuesday that the moves would allow Netflix to focus on its core business of producing TV shows and films aimed at making the service a must-have for consumers. Some analysts said incoming content chief Peter Rice will help improve Netflix's film and television slate by sharpening its focus on prestige programming and drawing on his relationships with top creative talent. "His industry relationships could prove valuable in attracting and retaining top filmmakers, especially following the departures of creators such as the Duffer Brothers, Shawn Levy, and Noah Baumbach," Citizens analyst Matthew Condon said. "Rice’s extensive experience overseeing live sports could support a more ambitious approach to premium sports programming, further enhancing Netflix’s value proposition." ANALYSTS CUT BACK EXPECTATIONS More than 20 brokerages have cut their price targets on the stock following the results, according to LSEG data. If current losses hold, the streaming giant is on track to lose about $13 billion in market value. BofA Global Research analysts said the leadership change and layoffs were "a signal that management is focused on improving content output and creative hit rates." Netflix trades at nearly 18.3 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, compared with 14.76 times for Walt Disney (DIS.N) and 6.26 times for Comcast (CMCSA.O) .

item.title: Putin agrees to resume 3-way peace talks with Ukraine and US
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two. The negotiations in a grand imperial palace in St Petersburg, the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of [USN:L8N4670PP TEXT:"Stephen Hubbard, a retired US school teacher"] held in Russia whom US President Trump had asked the Kremlin chief to release. Wednesday's encounter unfolded amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications. The latest talks also came more than two years since Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours. The Kremlin said the new 3-way peace talks, which would be at a technical level, could take place in Abu Dhabi and would be focused on how to guarantee the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war ended. They could begin sometime on or after November 10, it said. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran . The Kremlin was less upbeat, however, about the outcome of talks Witkoff had held a day earlier in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the leaders of Finland and Norway, and European and NATO representatives. Witkoff told Putin the talks had been characterised by "some degree of momentum" and a US official said Ukraine had brought [USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"new ideas and proposals"]. "These nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the St Petersburg meeting - which lasted nearly three hours. POSSIBLE MEETING BETWEEN TRUMP, PUTIN AND XI Ukraine and Russia remain far apart when it comes to the terms of any possible peace deal, though Trump has recently intensified pressure on Ukraine to strike some kind of a deal. He said on Tuesday it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing." Putin also used Wednesday's talks to offer to help Trump deal with Iran, saying Russia had a decades-long relationship with Tehran which it has repeatedly offered to leverage to address US concerns about Iran's nuclear programme. Putin told Witkoff it was possible and necessary to get a deal with Tehran, the Kremlin said. Russia could also supply vast quantities of fertiliser to the United States to help US farmers, the Russian president told Witkoff. [USN:L1N4650BJ TEXT:"A potential meeting in China next month"] with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was also discussed. The Kremlin said Beijing was already preparing what it said would be the first meeting of its kind in history. 'NEW IDEAS' Putin has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, no NATO membership for Kyiv, and an overall peace deal rather than a temporary ceasefire. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy, was also present at the talks with Witkoff and the Kremlin said that major joint economic projects had been discussed, including some that were close to being realised. Witkoff said he had brought some documents with him containing various ideas for a potential peace deal for Putin to review, and that Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, also wanted to convey some ideas to Putin. Kushner later joined the meeting remotely by phone. Zelenskiy said he [USN:L1N4670EW TEXT:"hoped to discuss key issues"] on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump. The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskiy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile. FRAYING US-UKRAINE TIES US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections. Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system, though Zelenskiy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues. Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated on Wednesday that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink.

item.title: EU will propose new tools to protect market, von der Leyen says
item.description: The European Commission will propose new measures to shield the EU from unfair competition from cheap imports, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commission will propose new measures to shield the EU from unfair competition from cheap imports, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday. A new instrument should enable EU countries to "immediately" limit access to the single market when surges in cheap imports threaten European industries, von der Leyen said in a speech in the European Parliament. "Competitiveness depends on our companies being able to compete on fair terms globally," she said. Von der Leyen said the Commission would also propose a "solidarity package", which should help countries that face specific trade threats. "In a world where economic power is increasingly used as a weapon, Europe must use its economic strength to defend its interests together," von der Leyen said.

item.title: Former Hungarian central bank chief Matolcsy detained in probe into loss of bank funds
item.description: Former Hungarian central bank governor Gyorgy Matolcsy was detained on Wednesday in an investigation into foundations set up by the bank during his tenure, which prosecutors say caused significant financial losses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Hungarian central bank governor Gyorgy Matolcsy was detained on Wednesday in an investigation into foundations set up by the bank during his tenure, which prosecutors say caused significant financial losses. The case involves a network of foundations and companies the central bank set up under Matolcsy. Since early 2025, prosecutors and police have been examining how more than 266 billion forints ($817 million) of central bank money moved through them. Prosecutors say this caused a particularly significant financial loss. The investigation began after a State Audit Office report raised concerns about investments made by a foundation set up by the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) and by Optima Investment Ltd, which managed the foundation's assets. "As part of the investigation ... today the Office questioned and detained former NBH governor Gyorgy Matolcsy and his accomplices as suspect," prosecutors said. They said they initiated an international arrest warrant against two more people, adding that Matolcsy refused to testify in the case. Matolcsy's lawyer, Pal Batki, told Reuters his client had been detained. "The suspicion against my client can be summarized as a very complex set of allegations, which we have not yet had the opportunity to fully review and process," he said. News site Telex, citing Batki, said Matolcsy was questioned over suspected fraud causing significant financial losses and the use of a forged private document. He said that prosecutors were seeking to arrest the former governor, and a court would decide on that this week. Matolcsy said in April that the bank had no legal mandate to interfere in the foundations' operations because they "were acting independently". Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who ousted Viktor Orban in an election in April, has said the central bank's past operations must be investigated, and his ruling party has also set up a parliamentary committee for that purpose. In May, Hungarian prosecutors and police [USN:L8N4260PC TEXT:"seized"] some 92 billion forints ($300 million) in funds and securities as part of a money-laundering investigation involving foundations set up by the central bank years ago. Prosecutors said that in 2014, under Matolcsy, the NBH established the Pallas Athene Foundations and gave them public money from the central bank's exchange rate gains. On February 28, 2025, Matolcsy's penultimate working day as central bank governor, a private equity fund represented by Optima concluded what prosecutors called a sham securities lending agreement, they said. Prosecutors said the agreement aimed at transferring control over the foundation's assets "to a circle of persons over whom Matolcsy would continue to influence after the expiry of his mandate as Governor, with the aim of enabling him and his son to make investments with the assets for their own purposes in order to make a profit." ($1 = 325.4200 forints)

item.title: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble
item.description: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, Leo Marchandon, Kanjyik Ghosh, Rajveer Pardesi
item.content:encoded: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems. Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes to vulnerabilities that had quietly been lurking in their software for years until they were uncovered using AI, saying that all users were "encouraged to update immediately." With tech firms warning that some hackers were already exploiting the flaws, government agencies across Europe were among those that took sites offline as a precaution. Because a fix is now public and artificial intelligence tools are able to reverse engineer the bug with little effort, experts said they were bracing for a wave of intrusions as hackers jumped to get ahead of fixes. AI was powering a "race to exploit," said Costin Raiu, co-founder of cybersecurity research and incident response firm TLP:Black. He said the next step was the "mass compromise of every vulnerable web server on the internet." PHP — a language that dates back to the early 1990s and initially stood for "Personal Home Page" — underpins huge parts of the public-facing web and is baked into WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento sites, meaning that any [USN:L6N467127 TEXT:"critical vulnerability"] potentially has enormous knock-on consequences. "All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable," said Tiffany Farriss, the interim chief executive of the Drupal Association. "This issue impacts the majority of the Internet." Cybersecurity agencies in Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. The operator of the online encyclopedia Wikipedia also said it had taken down an unspecified number of systems until they could be safely patched. Even some world leaders, who don't typically get involved with software updates, weighed in. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a post on X said website owners should "check whether your live site uses PHP and prepare to apply the new fix." BUG FOUND WITH AI The flaw in PHP was discovered using artificial intelligence, Alphabet-owned (GOOGL.O) cybersecurity company Wiz said in a blog post . The vulnerabilities remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade and would have been extraordinarily complicated for a human hacker to have taken advantage of, the post said. "Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale," it said. "With AI this is no longer a barrier." Wiz said its research relied on Wiz Atlas, its autonomous AI vulnerability research tool, as well as Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz said it coordinated with the PHP team, OpenAI, and the cybersecurity company Calif on the discovery of the vulnerability and patch verification. The company said it also partnered with Google Cloud, Cloudflare (NET.N) , Amazon's (AMZN.O) AWS, Microsoft (MSFT.O) , WordPress.com operator Automattic, and other companies such as Fastly (FSLY.O) , Akamai (AKAM.O) , Imperva, and Vercel to protect customers and prepare mitigations. In a statement, the White House said it was made aware of the flaw on Friday. "This discovery demonstrates exactly why American leadership in SI is so critical," the White House said, referring to President Donald Trump's preferred term for artificial intelligence. "This is American innovation strengthening our national security.” CRITICAL SOFTWARE PHP is a programming language used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP assembles the content and sends it to the browser. It is free, open-source software maintained by volunteers. Because of its ubiquity — PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs — and because the vulnerabilities are considered so dangerous, experts are anxious about a potentially vast pool of sitting ducks. AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have [USN:L6N46118G TEXT:"proliferated in recent weeks"], would only make things worse, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London. "The scale is huge, and with AI exploitation may happen instantly, on a large scale," Olejnik said. The risk is particularly acute for small websites run by individuals or organisations with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly manage the underlying servers. Security experts said such sites could take longer to patch and remain exposed well after fixes become available. MASS OUTAGES In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites for the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites. Danish municipal IT company Kombit said it had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform. Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure." France's Interior Ministry said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance. Japanese cloud service provider Sakura Internet said on Wednesday it had suspended a database appliance function.

item.title: Strong earnings help European shares erase nearly all losses from French unrest
item.description: European shares rose on Wednesday, recouping nearly all of their losses since the weekend turmoil in France as strong earnings encouraged investors to look past the economic and political uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: European shares rose on Wednesday, recouping nearly all of their losses since the weekend turmoil in France as strong earnings encouraged investors to look past the economic and political uncertainty. The pan-European STOXX 600 index (.STOXX) added 0.92% and closed at 644.49 points, led by a 20% jump in Randstad (RAND.AS) after the Dutch recruiter's management [USN:L6N4670AP TEXT:"struck a cheerful tone"] for 2027 following quarterly sales and profit beats. Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica's (ESLX.PA) 15.5% jump post earnings also helped the benchmark, and pushed luxury stocks (.STXLUXP) to their highest in more than five weeks. The gains show that solid corporate earnings are still capable of bolstering markets even as macroeconomic uncertainty persists, and vindicate investors who had counted on results to keep stocks afloat. Earnings this quarter have also shown unusual breadth. Third-quarter earnings for the STOXX 600 are expected to grow at one of the fastest rates in years, according to LSEG data. FRENCH STOCKS REBOUND France's CAC 40 index (.FCHI) rose for the first time this week, ending 1% higher. Riots erupted over the weekend in the euro zone's second-largest economy, battering sentiment. France's [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"government said it would ensure"] a massive deployment of troops to control the violence, but investors advocated caution. "The politics would sort of continue to be a bit of an anchor on shorter-term performance," said Ben Gutteridge, head of market insights at Invesco. The European automobiles sector (.SXAP) fell 1.7%, leading losses. The STOXX 600 is up about 8% so far this year but remains below the yearly highs it touched in August, as inflation concerns and political jitters have weighed on the index. It has underperformed its US peer, the S&P 500 (.SPX) , which is up 12.7%. On Wednesday, Carrefour (CARR.PA) dropped 13.8% after the supermarket chain [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"cut its annual earnings forecast"], saying riots, looting and curfews had raised costs and disrupted trading at its stores. Tyre maker Michelin (MICP.PA) declined 7.2% after reporting a drop in nine-month sales. DSV (DSV.CO) gained 15% after the transport and logistics firm reported a rise in its third-quarter revenue. Investors are also awaiting results from SAP (SAPG.DE) on Wednesday, and Nokia (NOKIA.HE) and Barclays (BARC.L) on Thursday for clues on positioning. On the data front, British inflation [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"rose more than expected"] last month, bolstering expectations that the Bank of England could raise interest rates at its November meeting. UK's FTSE 100 (.FTSE) ended 0.19% higher. "Underlying pressures remain worrying. Strong growth and stable labour-market slack strengthen the case for multiple hikes," economists at Pantheon Macroeconomics wrote.

item.title: Getty Images files for US bankruptcy, advances restructuring plan
item.description: Getty Images filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Wednesday, formalizing restructuring plans unveiled more than a week ago as part of its move to go private.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Getty Images (GETY.PK) filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Wednesday, formalizing restructuring plans unveiled more than a week ago as part of its move to go private. Last week, Getty [USN:L6N45Y0UP TEXT:"announced"] plans to file for bankruptcy, marking a major reset after its planned merger with rival Shutterstock (SSTK.N) collapsed under the weight of heavy debt and growing competition from AI-generated imagery Getty said the affiliates of the Getty family and Koch Equity Development, which committed to provide up to $533 million in new equity, will own 100% of the company after the restructuring Getty said on Wednesday it launched a solicitation process to secure formal approval for its reorganization plan announced last week The visual-content provider said it will continue operating in the ordinary course throughout the process, with no impact on content contributors, partners, customers, employees or vendors Getty Images expects to complete the restructuring by year-end In a filing at the Delaware bankruptcy court, the company listed both estimated assets and liabilities in the range of $1 billion to $10 billion Getty, which competes with Reuters and the Associated Press in providing photos and videos for editorial use, said financing from Koch Equity Development of up to $143 million would support the restructuring process

item.title: Micron faces strike from one Taiwan union after deal with another
item.description: A union representing workers at a Micron plant in Taiwan said it would proceed with a planned strike on Thursday, even as the US memory chipmaker reached a deal with a separate union at a larger site.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Yee Lee
item.content:encoded: A union representing workers at a Micron (MU.O) plant in Taiwan said it would proceed with a planned strike on Thursday, even as the US memory chipmaker reached a deal with a separate union at a larger site. The AI boom has boosted memory chipmakers including Micron, Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix, (.MSPMHYNX) while also sharpening worker demands for a greater share of profits. The Taoyuan union said Micron had failed to provide specific figures for a proposed profit-sharing scheme during negotiations held on Wednesday. It said union representatives would stage a 24-hour strike outside the company's Taoyuan facility from 9 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Thursday. "Micron remains hopeful that both sides will continue their dialogue," the Idaho-based company said in a statement. Micron, the world's third-largest memory chipmaker, employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan, a key production base for its dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips, which store data temporarily in devices from smartphones to servers, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips used in AI servers. The Taoyuan union's announcement injected fresh uncertainty into a dispute that appeared to be cooling down hours earlier. Earlier on Wednesday, Micron and the Taichung union, which represents workers at the company's largest Taiwan site, said in a joint statement they had signed an agreement and would withdraw from mediation talks planned for Thursday. They did not disclose the terms, saying each side would communicate details separately to affected employees. The Taoyuan union had originally scheduled the strike to coincide with the mediation talks. Taoyuan focuses on front-end DRAM wafer manufacturing, while Taichung produces advanced DRAM and HBM chips and handles packaging and testing, said Ellie Wang, an analyst at market research firm TrendForce. The effect of the Taoyuan strike would depend on which production lines and key personnel were affected, Wang said. A strike would not necessarily mean a full shutdown if maintenance, process monitoring and abnormality handling were adequately staffed, she added. If the action lasts only one day and critical production remains normal, the impact on Micron's supply and global markets would likely be limited, Wang said.

item.title: Gold steadies near one-week low as oil-driven inflation fears grow
item.description: Gold prices hovered near a one-week low on Wednesday as a rally in oil prices stoked inflation fears linked to Middle East tensions, with investors looking ahead to next week's Federal Reserve meeting.
item.dc:creator: Anushree Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Gold prices hovered near a one-week low on Wednesday as a rally in oil prices stoked inflation fears linked to Middle East tensions, with investors looking ahead to next week's Federal Reserve meeting. Spot gold was up 0.1% at $4,127.31 per ounce by 11:10 am EDT (1510 GMT) after hitting its lowest since October 15 in earlier trade. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.1% to $4,145.20 per ounce. "I think the market is currently expecting one 25-basis-point rate hike this year, but probably not until December. The likelihood of an October rate hike has dropped pretty significantly," said Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals. "I think gold prices will be range-bound for the time being. But I think the bias remains to the downside." Attention is turning to the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 policy meeting and next week's US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report for clues on future rate moves. Markets are pricing in an 88% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Nearly all economists [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"surveyed by Reuters"] expect the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady this month before delivering a hike in December, as policymakers opt for patience despite persistent inflation pressures that would otherwise call for stronger action. Although gold is traditionally considered an inflation hedge, higher rates dent its appeal as investors prefer yield-bearing assets. Oil prices rose more than $2 on Wednesday, with Brent crude holding around $108 a barrel, as Iran's comments dimmed hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough with the United States. "I would still believe in the short term, gold is in consolidation mode. So whenever we go below 4,100, it's bottoming out because there is buying interest, but the upside remains limited as long as the conflict in the Middle East is somehow still a topic," said Giovanni Staunovo, an analyst at UBS. Among other metals, spot silver slid 0.9% to $57.46 per ounce, platinum fell 1.1% to $1,630.03 and palladium dropped 1.2% to $1,089.73.

item.title: Trump, in North Carolina, says Republicans will defy midterm odds
item.description: With his approval rating at record lows, President Donald Trump attempted to defy political gravity in a pep rally in North Carolina on Tuesday, urging voters to support his favored Senate candidate in a race some Republican groups have already given up on.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: With his approval rating at record lows, President Donald Trump attempted to defy political gravity in a pep rally in North Carolina on Tuesday, urging voters to support his favored Senate candidate in a race some Republican groups have already given up on. Trump has embarked on a campaign blitz ahead of the November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], traveling more than 29,000 miles (46,671 km) since late September to boost Republican candidates. His second stop in North Carolina in as many months was a signal of how much is at stake in this southern state. Polls show former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper with a [USN:L6N4620WO TEXT:"commanding lead"] over Republican Michael Whatley, a former senior party official, in a Senate race that could help decide the balance of power in Washington. The two are running to fill the seat of retiring Republican Thom Tillis, a one-time Trump ally, who split with the president over his landmark tax bill and defense policy. Tillis told Politico in a Tuesday interview that his fellow Republicans were headed toward “a train wreck” and a "whoop ass" in November. But Trump, speaking in the eastern city of Greenville on Tuesday night, predicted Whatley would prove the doubters wrong. "I think you're gonna see some amazing results," he told hundreds of supporters who gathered on the grounds of the local airport. "They never poll us right. We have more spirit." 'WE NEED YOU' Trump won North Carolina in each of his three presidential runs, but Democrats are banking on a breakthrough performance this year, with polls showing a clear majority of Americans dissatisfied with rising prices and the war in Iran. The president's approval rating has [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"fallen to 31%,"] according to the latest Reuters/Ipsos survey, the lowest mark at any point during his two terms in office. In early voting in North Carolina, Democrats have cast more ballots than Republicans by a two-to-one margin, according to state data. Republican candidates on Tuesday night implored voters to turn out early. "This is a Republican majority district," said Laurie Buckhout, a Trump-backed candidate running for a congressional seat in a mostly rural eastern district. “We have the momentum. We have the message. Now we need you." Republicans hold 10 of the state's 14 House seats, but a handful of districts are viewed as battlegrounds this cycle — and have attracted significant spending. Buckhout's race against Democratic Representative Don Davis has drawn $21 million in outside money since September 1, making it the third most expensive contest in the country, according to a Reuters analysis of campaign filings. In the state's mountainous west, outside groups have spent $14.5 million on the race between Democrat Jamie Ager and Republican Jennifer Balkcom. Whatley, by contrast, has largely been abandoned by the national party apparatus. The Senate Leadership Fund, the primary PAC supporting Republican candidates for the upper chamber, cut off spending in North Carolina earlier this month as Cooper posted double-digit leads in poll after poll. 'TIGHTEN THAT SHIP UP' Trump's popularity has cratered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel, triggering a surge in gasoline and diesel prices. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy, Reuters/Ipsos has found, including 37% of self-identified Republicans. Taylor Smith, who described herself as a housewife in Greenville, told Reuters she had only ever voted Republican, but the drama of the Trump administration had her thinking twice. Disorganization within the White House was bleeding into policy, she said, revealing Trump’s lack of focus. “Anything good that could be happening is being co-opted by the tomfoolery that's just going on,” Smith said. "I hate these gas prices," she added, urging the president to “tighten that ship up.” As he has in events across the country, Trump heralded what he said were new local investments on Tuesday night. Sibelco, an industrial minerals mining and processing company, was expanding its operations in North Carolina, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced on stage without providing specifics. In a statement to Reuters, Sibelco said "we are awaiting the official communication from the US Government and are therefore not in a position to comment." Trump said the US Defense Department would also invest $1.5 billion in semiconductor chip production in North Carolina, but did not say where or how the money would be spent. Toward the end of his speech, the president [USN:S8N41C0VN TEXT:"repeated his promise"] to give $5,000 to every US adult should Republicans maintain their hold on Congress. "If we lose," he said, "you get nothing."

item.title: Stocks rise with upbeat earnings; France's 10-year bond yield hits 5% mark
item.description: Major stock indexes climbed on Wednesday as results and forecasts lifted sentiment about the earnings outlook, while France's 10-year bond yield hit 5% for the first time since 2002 amid concern about the outlook for the country's economy.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch, Dhara Ranasinghe
item.content:encoded: Major stock indexes climbed on Wednesday as results and forecasts lifted sentiment about the earnings outlook, while France's 10-year bond yield hit 5% for the first time since 2002 amid concern about the outlook for the country's economy. Shares of SpaceX (SPCX.O) [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"also shot up"] about 10% after Elon Musk said late on Tuesday that a merger of his two companies SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea." SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company. Shares in companies in Japan and Taiwan that are suppliers to Tesla and SpaceX advanced as well. Super Micro (SMCI.O) shares [USN:L4N4661QH TEXT:"jumped"] more than 9% after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates. Investors have been worried about the strength of the AI trade and swings in prices of government bonds ahead of the third-quarter reporting period, with [USN:L6N45Z12J TEXT:"AI-related shares"] selling off recently. "A lot of the concerns that we had over the last few weeks that sent the market lower are being alleviated," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in New York. Earnings, he said, "are coming in mixed to stronger than expected. That's a big relief because... tech stocks fell hard last week on fears that the AI party is over." In addition, US bond yields have been falling after their recent run higher, and US interest rate hike expectations have been coming down, he said. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes was down 1.47 basis points at 5.102%, from 5.117% late on Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 76.77 points, or 0.15%, to 52,572.65, the S&P 500 (.SPX) rose 27.15 points, or 0.35%, to 7,739.72 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) was up 226.91 points, or 0.86%, at 26,651.94. Meta (META.O) and Tesla are due to report results after the bell. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) rose 3.98 points, or 0.35%, to 1,134.38. The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index rose 0.84%. In Asia, Korean stocks (.KS11) gained 3%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 (.N225) rose almost 1%. Shares of South Korean artificial intelligence infrastructure company Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) [USN:P8N44T04P TEXT:"surged"] almost 30%, rebounding from a slump in its market debut on Tuesday. In addition, Australian data center operator NextDC (NXT.AX) shed nearly half of its market capitalization on Wednesday after sharply cutting [USN:L4N4661TS TEXT:"revenue forecasts"] for the year ahead and putting future developments on hold, extending the burst of negative sentiment towards global AI stocks. UNEASE IN FRANCE France's bond yields rose again as investors took stock of the [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"widespread protests"] across the country that have piled pressure on a government already struggling to shore up its finances. Its 10-year bond yield hit a new 24-year high above 5%. The premium on French yields over benchmark 10-year German Bunds has also been edging back toward early October's 15-year high of nearly 160 bps. French supermarket operator Carrefour (CARR.PA) fell 13% after it cut its [USN:L6N4670H2 TEXT:"guidance"] due to the recent protests. The euro was down 0.1% at $1.1226. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar weakened 0.06% to 158.06. Investors awaited next week's Federal Reserve meeting. Elsewhere, the Australian dollar gained after Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser told a Citi conference that the inflation outlook looked "materially worse." The Aussie was last up 0.24% versus the greenback at $0.702. Indonesia's central bank [USN:L4N466083 TEXT:"held"] its main interest rate unchanged on Wednesday, but raised its deposit facility rate by 25 basis points and cut banks' reserve requirement ratio by 2 percentage points to support liquidity and lending after markets were roiled by an MSCI warning last week that Indonesian stocks could be excluded from its major benchmarks. In the oil market, prices were mixed. US data showed a larger-than-expected draw in oil stocks. US crude was last down 0.15% at $97.67 a barrel, while Brent rose to $109.12 per barrel, up 0.3% on the day.

item.title: US high court rulings have been 'destructive to democracy,' Justice Kagan says
item.description: US Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan on Tuesday said the court's conservative majority has undermined democracy and "created a race to the bottom" in how congressional districts are drawn.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: US Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan on Tuesday said the court's conservative majority has undermined democracy and "created a race to the bottom" in how congressional districts are drawn. Kagan, one of the court's three liberals, told students at Catholic University's law school that the conservatives have enabled increased political polarization by not reining in partisan gerrymandering, which involves states redrawing the boundaries of electoral districts based on the partisan leanings of voters to boost a political party's candidates. In recent years, Kagan said, "both political parties have been engaged in a race to the bottom in terms of doing these partisan gerrymanders, effectively depriving masses of citizens of their rights to voting equality." Partisan gerrymandering is driving political candidates "toward the extremes, because the only thing anybody has to worry about anymore is being primaried," Kagan said. "It is making what I think is unfortunately a too polarized country even more so," Kagan said. "In this election, and the next election, we are seeing large states with substantial numbers of people who vote for Republicans and who vote for Democrats, and the states are going to be tried to turn all red or all blue in a way that I think is very destructive to our democracy." The court, which has a 6-3 conservative majority, in April [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"gutted"] a pillar of the Voting Rights Act, a landmark 1965 civil rights law that aimed to prevent racial discrimination in voting. That ruling prompted a frenzied round of [USN:L1N41P12P TEXT:"redistricting"] across the South to eliminate US House of Representatives districts where Black voters make up a majority or near-majority, as Republican-led states scrambled to take advantage of the decision. President Donald Trump's Republican Party is seeking to retain control of Congress in the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"November midterm elections"]. At Trump's urging, Republican-governed Texas redrew its electoral map last year in an effort to flip Democratic-held US House seats, while Democratic-led California then reconfigured its map to target Republican-held House seats. Kagan, an appointee of former Democratic President Barack Obama, said the court's conservatives did not appreciate the real-world impact of their April voting rights decision, or their [USN:L1N4310Y4 TEXT:"June decision"] that struck down a cap on the amount of money parties can spend on campaigns with input from candidates. "I think part of the reason why the court got it wrong was a lack of the appropriate concern or understanding of the consequences of their decisions," Kagan said. “I do think in all these areas the court has blinded itself to the very deleterious effects of their rulings on how the political system works and has created a democracy that doesn’t work as well as it should,” she added. Kagan added that the June decision on campaign finance regulation has created opportunities for donors to corrupt candidates. "The one place where the court has allowed campaign finance regulation to operate is to prevent quid pro quo corruption, kind of money for favors, and the court never seems to see the opportunities for doing exactly that," Kagan said. “I think you know the people of America look around this political system and think that all this money, chasing all these political candidates, is a nightmare, and they’re right,” she said.

item.title: Investors flood to Jio IPO on day one of India's largest offering
item.description: Investors flocked to Jio Platforms’ $3.2 billion IPO on Wednesday, with bids covering the shares on offer in under two hours and reaching 3.16 times by the end of the first day, in India’s largest IPO and the first by Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance in 20 years.
item.dc:creator: Vibhuti Sharma, Aditya Kalra, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Investors flocked to Jio Platforms’ (JIOP.NS) $3.2 billion IPO on Wednesday, with bids covering the shares on offer in under two hours and reaching 3.16 times by the end of the first day, in India’s largest IPO and the first by Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance in 20 years. The IPO has been seen as a major test of global appetite for new share offerings at a time when investors have sharpened their scrutiny of AI-related companies, which some analysts say could see them pivoting away from the technology. Almost 90% of Jio Platforms' revenue comes from its telecoms business. With backing from Meta (META.O) , Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and institutional investors, Jio Platforms (JIOP.NS) is home to India's biggest telecoms company with more than 500 million subscribers, making it the world's second-largest telecoms operator in a single country after China Mobile (600941.SS) . Institutional investors covered the allotted tranche in 10 minutes, while the overall book was filled within 100 minutes, said two people close to the IPO. "It's the fastest in the history of India," one said. The investor rush comes even as big IPOs in India generally start slowly, with institutions often waiting until the final hours to bid. In other big IPOs, the National Stock Exchange of India's (NSEI.BO) share sale recently was only 42% subscribed on its first day, and Hyundai Motor India's (HYUN.NS) only 18%. Aishvarya Dadheech, founder at Fident Asset Management, said Jio's rapid IPO bidding was surprising given large IPOs in India typically get fully subscribed later on, adding: "Jio has changed India's telecom landscape and (the IPO) offers a very reasonable valuation with strong fundamentals". Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began in 2016 with a bet that Indians would use the internet far more if it cost almost nothing. It rapidly took market share from rivals such as Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and Vodafone Idea (VODA.NS) by offering cheap data and free voice calls. The IPO values Jio Platforms at up to $108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India's biggest companies by market capitalisation when trading starts on October 28. Bharti Airtel's market capitalisation on Wednesday stood at $123.38 billion. QUICK BIDS Institutional investors have so far shown more enthusiasm than retail, with qualified institutional buyers subscribing 9.42 times their reserved portion in the IPO, exchange data showed, while retail investors, for whom around a third of the issue is reserved, have so far bid for 0.73 times their quota. New bids, however, were not coming in as fast as the early morning hours, according to live stock exchange data. For many Indians, Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) , which listed in 1977 and has businesses ranging from retail to oil, has been a long-term wealth generator and a savings vehicle that helped pay for a child's education or a wedding. Since 1990, for which LSEG data is available, Reliance's Mumbai-traded shares have risen around 330-fold. Jio Platforms this week [USN:L1N46509C TEXT:"allotted"] shares worth $853 million to more than 200 global and domestic investors including Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock (BLK.N) after the reserved portion drew bids totalling more than $25 billion. Retail investors, as well as employees and shareholders of Reliance, are participating in the offering that closes on Friday and has a 1,065 to 1,119 rupees per share price range. FESTIVE LAUNCH DATE The IPO is the first from Reliance since 2006. Ambani first promised a listing within five years in 2019, and the plans were also delayed [USN:L1N3T60EG TEXT:"in 2025"]. A filing for as early as March was pushed back after the Iran war dampened IPO appetite. Jio Platforms is pitching its IPO during an ongoing Hindu festive season, which is considered auspicious for purchases, but at a time when Indian markets have remained subdued in recent weeks. Reliance paid its more than 400,000 employees their salaries about 15 days early this month, and the company helped facilitate share account-opening services in recent weeks to those interested in applying for the IPO, a person in the industry with direct knowledge of the situation said. Reliance did not respond to a request for comment. Jio Platforms earned about $3.2 billion [USN:L1N46005C TEXT:"in profit"] on $15.5 billion of revenue in the year to March. The firm plans to use up to $2.89 billion of the proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at its telecoms unit. The rest will be used for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure, Jio's IPO prospectus showed.

item.description: L'Europe finit dans le vert, portée par les résultats
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe finit dans le vert, portée par les résultats PARIS, 21 octobre (Reuters) - Les Bourses européennes ont terminé dans le vert mercredi une séance au cours de laquelle les investisseurs ont privilégié les solides résultats des entreprises, faisant fi des tensions dans l'obligataire en zone euro à la suite des craintes sur le niveau de l'endettement des Etats, en particulier celui de la France. Edenred-Le dépassement des attentes au T3 peine à convaincre, le titre baisse 21 octobre (Reuters) - Edenred a publié mercredi un revenu total supérieur aux attentes au titre du troisième trimestre, le spécialiste français des titres-restaurant citant la croissance continue de son segment mobilité. Covivio: Hausse de 2,7% des revenus sur les neufs premiers mois 21 octobre (Reuters) - Covivio a fait état mercredi d'une croissance de 2,7% de ses revenus à périmètre constant sur les neufs premiers mois de son exercice, soutenus entre autres par les hausses de loyers et les gains de taux d'occupation ainsi que les revenus variables des hôtels. FDJ United abaisse ses objectifs de CA et de produit brut des jeux 21 octobre (Reuters) - FDJ United a annoncé mercredi un abaissement de ses objectifs annuels, tablant désormais sur une baisse comprise entre 1% et 3% ("low-single digit") du produit brut des jeux (PBJ) et sur un déclin d'environ 5% ("mid-single digit") de son chiffre d'affaires pour l'exercice 2026. Le rendement de l'OAT à 10 ans atteint 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002 21 octobre (Reuters) - Le rendement de l'obligation souveraine française à 10 ans a atteint mercredi le seuil psychologique de 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002, ce qui constitue un nouveau signe de l'inquiétude des investisseurs quant à la capacité de la deuxième économie de la zone euro à réduire son déficit. Moncler: CA stable au T3, freiné par la baisse des dépenses touristiques en Europe MILAN, 21 octobre (Reuters) - Moncler a fait état mercredi d'un chiffre d'affaires globalement stable au troisième trimestre à taux directeur constants, le groupe italien de vêtements de luxe subissant les effets d'un recul en Europe lié à la baisse des dépenses touristiques. item.content:encoded: France: Macron dénonce les commentaires des dirigeants étrangers sur les manifestations 21 octobre (Reuters) - Emmanuel Macron a dénoncé mercredi les commentaires émanant de "dirigeants étrangers" en campagne électorale à propos des manifestations émaillées de violences du 17 octobre en France, à l'occasion d'une tournée dans les pays du Golfe. France: Vinted retire de la vente les articles soupçonnés d'être volés en marge des manifestations L'application dédiée à l'achat et à la vente de vêtements d'occasion Vinted a annoncé lundi avoir renforcé les contrôles sur les annonces suspectes et supprimé celles revendant des biens pillés en marge des manifestations de ce weekend en France. France et Allemagne d'accord sur un plan pour l'automobile La France et l'Allemagne ont annoncé vendredi un accord sur une "approche commune" visant à garantir l'avenir de l'industrie automobile européenne, avec un accent mis à la fois sur la transition énergétique et sur une production des véhicules en Europe. Les tortues caouannes, sentinelles du réchauffement en Méditerranée Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique.
